General. The Company's primary sources of funds are deposits; amortization, prepayments and maturities of outstanding loans; other short- term investments; and funds provided from operations.
paragraphs: Citizens Community Bancorp, Inc. (the "Company") is a Maryland corporation organized in 2004. The Company is a bank holding company and is subject to regulation by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency ("OCC") and by the Federal Reserve Bank. Our primary activities consist of holding the stock of our wholly-owned subsidiary bank, Citizens Community Federal N.A. (the "Bank"), and providing commercial, agricultural and consumer banking activities through the Bank. At December 31, 2025, we had approximately $1.782 billion in total assets, $1.524 billion in deposits, and $187.9 million in equity.

The Bank is a federally chartered National Bank serving customers in Wisconsin and Minnesota through 21 full-service branch locations. Its primary markets include the Chippewa Valley Region in Wisconsin, the Twin Cities and Mankato markets in Minnesota, and various rural communities around these areas. The Bank offers traditional community banking services to businesses, Agricultural operators and consumers, including one-to-four family residential mortgages.

We maintain a website at www.ccf.us. We make available through that website, free of charge, copies of our Annual Reports on Form 10-K, Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q, Current Reports on Form 8-K, proxy statements for our annual stockholders' meetings and amendments to those reports or documents, as soon as reasonably practicable after we electronically file those materials with, or furnish them to, the Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC"). We are not including the information contained on or available through our website as a part of, or incorporating such information by reference into, this Annual Report on Form 10-K. The SEC also maintains a website at www.sec.gov that contains reports, proxy statements and other information regarding SEC registrants.

We offer a variety of loan products including commercial real estate loans, commercial and industrial (C&I) loans, agricultural real estate loans, agricultural operating loans, residential mortgages, home equity lines-of-credit and consumer loans. We make real estate, consumer, commercial and agricultural loans in accordance with the basic lending policies established by Bank management and approved by our Board of Directors. We focus our lending activities on individual consumers and small commercial borrowers within our market areas. Our lending has been historically concentrated primarily within Wisconsin and Minnesota. Competitive and economic pressures exist in our lending markets, and recent and any future developments in (a) the general economy, (b) real estate lending markets, and (c) the banking regulatory environment could have a material adverse effect on our business and operations. These factors may impact the credit quality of our existing loan portfolio, or adversely impact our ability to originate sufficient high quality loans in the future.

Our total gross outstanding loans, before net deferred loan costs and unamortized discounts on acquired loans, as of December 31, 2025, were $1.343 billion, consisting of $1.074 billion in commercial/agricultural real estate loans, $139.3 million in C&I/agricultural operating loans, $123.8 million in residential mortgage loans and $6.2 million in consumer installment loans. See Item 7; "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations", under the heading "Balance Sheet Analysis" for further analysis of our loan portfolio.

We maintain a portfolio of investments, consisting primarily of mortgage-backed securities, asset-backed securities, U.S. Government sponsored agency securities and corporate debt securities. We attempt to balance our portfolio to manage interest rate risk, regulatory requirements, and liquidity needs while providing an appropriate rate of return commensurate with the risk of the investment. See Item 7; "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations", under the heading "Balance Sheet Analysis Investment Securities" for further analysis of our investment portfolio.

Deposits. We offer a broad range of deposit products through our branches, including demand deposits, various savings and money-market accounts and certificates of deposit. Deposits are insured by the Deposit Insurance Fund ("DIF") of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation ("FDIC") up to statutory limits. At December 31, 2025, our total deposits were $1.524 billion including interest bearing deposits of $1.260 billion and non-interest bearing deposits of $0.264 billion.

Borrowings. In addition to our primary sources of funds, we maintain access to additional sources of funds through borrowing, including FHLB borrowings, lines of credit with the Federal Reserve Bank, our Revolving Loan and our Federal Funds Purchased Lines of Credit. See Item 7; "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations", under the heading "Balance Sheet Analysis Federal Home Loan Bank (FHLB) advances and other borrowings" for further analysis of our borrowings.

We compete with other financial institutions and businesses both in attracting and retaining deposits and making loans in all of our principal markets. We believe the primary factors in competing for deposits are interest rates, personalized services, the quality and range of financial services, technology, convenient locations and office hours, and alternative delivery systems. One such delivery system is remote deposit capture for those commercial customers that are not conveniently located near one of our branches or mobile banking for retail customers. Competition for deposit products comes primarily from other banks, credit unions and non-bank competitors, including insurance companies, money market and mutual funds, and other investment alternatives. We believe the primary factors in competing for loans are interest rates, loan origination fees, and the quality and the range of lending services. Successful loan originations tend to depend not only on interest rate and terms of the loan but also on being responsive and flexible to the customer's needs. Competition for loans comes primarily from other banks, mortgage banking firms, credit unions, finance companies, leasing companies and other financial intermediaries. Some of our competitors are not subject to the same degree of regulation as that imposed on national banks or federally insured institutions, and these other institutions may be able to price loans and deposits more aggressively. We also face direct competition from other banks and their holding companies that have greater assets and resources than ours. However, we have been able to compete effectively with other financial institutions by building customer relationships with a focus on small-business solutions, including internet and mobile banking, electronic bill pay and remote deposit capture.

The banking industry is highly regulated, and the Company and the Bank are subject to numerous laws and regulations. As a bank holding company, the Company is subject to regulation, supervision and examination by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve (the "FRB"). The Bank is also subject to regulation, supervision and examination by the OCC. The Bank is a member of the Federal Reserve System and the Federal Home Loan Bank System. In addition, the Bank's deposit accounts are insured by the FDIC to the maximum extent permitted by law, and the FDIC has certain enforcement powers over the Bank.

The following is a brief summary of material statutes and regulations that affect the Company and the Bank. The following summary is not a complete discussion or analysis and is qualified in its entirety by reference to the statutes and regulations summarized below. The laws and regulations applicable to the Company and the Bank are subject to change.

headings: The impact of larger or similar-sized financial institutions encountering financial difficulties may adversely affect the Company's business, earnings and financial condition.
paragraphs: The risks described below are not the only risks we face. Additional risks that we do not yet know of or that we currently believe are immaterial may also impair our future business operations. If any of the events or circumstances described in the following risks actually occurs, our business, financial condition or results of operations could be materially adversely affected. In such cases, the trading price of our common stock could decline.

Our business may be adversely affected by conditions in the financial markets and economic conditions generally. We operate primarily in the Wisconsin and Minnesota markets. As a result, our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows are significantly impacted by changes in the economic conditions in those areas. In addition, our business is susceptible to broader economic trends within the United States economy. Economic conditions have a significant impact on the demand for our products and services, as well as the ability of our customers to repay loans, the value of the collateral securing loans and the stability of our deposit funding sources. A significant decline in general economic conditions caused by inflation, recession, trade policies, tariffs, unemployment, changes in securities markets, rate cuts by the Federal Reserve, changes in housing market prices, geopolitical uncertainties, natural disasters, pandemics and election outcomes or other factors could impact economic conditions and, in turn, could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.

Inflation may have an adverse impact on our business and on our customers. Inflation risk is the risk that the value of assets or income from investments will be worth less in the future as inflation decreases the value of money. The annual inflation rate as of December 2025 was 2.7% measured by consumer price index. Inflation increases the cost of goods and services we use in our business operations, such as electricity and other utilities, which increases our non-interest expenses. Furthermore, our customers are also affected by inflation and the rising costs of goods and services used in their households and businesses, which could have a negative impact on their ability to repay their loans with us or the willingness of businesses to take loans with us.

Geopolitical tensions, including current or anticipated impact of military conflicts, could adversely affect general economic industry conditions. Geopolitical tensions may affect our earnings. Adverse economic conditions may result from a variety of factors including domestic and global economic and political developments, including civil unrest, terrorism, foreign investment restrictions, various political or military action, such as the armed conflict between Ukraine and Russia and corresponding sanctions imposed by the United States and other countries or the conflict in the Middle East and the surrounding areas, geopolitical events (including China-Taiwan and U.S.-China relations), and new or evolving legal and regulatory requirements on business investment, hiring, migration, labor supply and global supply chains.

We are subject to higher lending risks with respect to our commercial and agricultural banking activities which could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations. Our loans include commercial and agricultural loans, which include loans secured by real estate as well as loans secured by personal property. Commercial real estate lending, including agricultural loans, typically involves higher loan principal amounts and the repayment of these loans is generally largely dependent on the successful operation of the property or the business conducted on the property securing the loan. Commercial real estate loans may be more adversely affected by conditions in the real estate markets or in the general economy. Agricultural operating loans carry significant risks as they may involve larger balances concentrated with a single borrower or group of related borrowers. In addition, repayment of such loans depends on the successful operation or management of the farm property securing the loan for which an operating loan is utilized. Farming operations may be affected by factors outside of the borrower's control, including adverse weather conditions, such as drought, hail or floods that can severely limit crop yields and declines in market prices for agricultural products. Furthermore, severe weather events such as catastrophic fire, tornado, or

other events could impact the markets that we serve and adversely impact our customers, such as hindering our borrowers' ability to timely repay their loans and diminish the value of the collateral held by us. Although the Bank manages lending risks through its underwriting and credit administration policies, no assurance can be given that such risks will not materialize, in which event, our financial condition, results of operations, cash flows and business prospects could be materially adversely affected.

paragraphs: The following discussion sets forth management's discussion and analysis of our results of operations for the year ended December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024, and our financial position as of December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024, respectively. The MD&A should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements, related notes, the selected financial data and the statistical information presented elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K for a more complete understanding of the following discussion and analysis. Unless otherwise noted, years refer to the Company's fiscal years ended December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024.

The following is a summary of some of the significant factors that affected our operating results for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, compared to the same 2024 period. In 2025, net interest income increased $4.7 million, due to: (1) the ongoing impact of lower short-term interest rates on the Bank's liability-sensitive balance sheet which lowered liability costs; (2) higher asset yields; partially offset by (3) the impact of lower interest income due to a smaller sized balance sheet. The Company recorded a $1.950 million provision for credit losses largely due to the impact of changes in credit quality, largely due to an increase in reserves on individually evaluated loans. The $3.175 million of negative provision for credit losses in 2024 was largely due to the impact of improving forecasted future economic conditions, as forecasted by Moody's, who the Company utilizes for economic forecasts and the impact of balance sheet optimization, which resulted in loan portfolio shrinkage. Non-interest income for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, compared to the same period in 2024 increased approximately $1.0 million. This increase was largely due to: (1) higher gains on equity securities; (2) higher gain on sale of loans, due to an increase in SBA gains and mortgage gains, with SBA being about two thirds of the increase; partially offset by (3) lower fee income on deposit activity, due to lower activity; and (4) a decrease in loan fees and service charges primarily due to lower fees collected on loan payoffs. Non-interest expense increased approximately 1.5% or $0.6 million primarily due to a $1.1 million increase in compensation due to higher incentive compensation and merit increases, partially offset by a decrease in other expense due to lower SBA recourse expense.

When comparing year-over-year results, changes in net interest income, provision for credit losses, non-interest income and non-interest expense are primarily due to the items discussed above. See the remainder of this section for a more thorough discussion. Unless otherwise stated, all monetary amounts in the tables (but not the narrative) set forth in this Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations, other than share, per share and capital ratio amounts, are stated in thousands.

We reported net income of $14.42 million for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, compared to net income of $13.75 million for the twelve months ended December 31, 2024. Diluted earnings per share were $1.46 for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, compared to $1.34 for the twelve months ended December 31, 2024. Return on average assets for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, was 0.82%, compared to 0.76% for the twelve months ended December 31, 2024. The return on average equity was 7.89% for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, and 7.84% for the comparable period in 2024.

The Company utilized a balance sheet optimization strategy in 2025, which resulted in the runoff of non-strategic loan relationships with the proceeds used to reduce all borrowings at the Bank and reductions in wholesale deposits.

Our consolidated financial statements have been prepared in conformity with U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles ("GAAP"). In connection with the preparation of our financial statements, we are required to make assumptions and estimates about future events and apply judgments that affect the reported amount of assets, liabilities, revenue, expenses, and the related disclosures. We base our assumptions, estimates and judgments on historical experience, current trends, and other factors that management believes to be relevant at the time our consolidated financial statements are prepared. Some of these estimates are more critical than others. Below is a discussion of our critical accounting estimates.

We utilize a loss estimation methodology and third-party model to determine our allowance for credit losses, under the guidance of ASU 2016-13, Financial Instruments - Credit Losses (Topic 326), "Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments". See also Notes 1 and 3 to the audited consolidated financial statements for further discussion of our adoption of ASU 2016-13.

Allowance for Credit Losses - Loans. We maintain an allowance for credit losses to absorb probable and inherent losses in our loan portfolio. The allowance is based on ongoing, quarterly assessments of the estimated lifetime losses in our loan portfolio. In evaluating the level of the allowance for credit losses, we consider the types of loans and the amount of loans in our loan portfolio, historical loss experience, adverse situations that may affect the borrower's ability to repay, the estimated value of any underlying collateral, prevailing economic conditions and other relevant factors determined by management. We follow all applicable regulatory guidance, including the "Interagency Policy Statement on Allowances for Credit Losses," issued by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, Department of the Treasury, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve, Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, and National Credit Union Administration. We believe that the Bank's Allowance for Credit Losses Policy conforms to all applicable regulatory requirements. However, based on periodic examinations by regulators, the amount of the allowance for credit losses recorded during a particular period may be adjusted.

Our determination of the allowance for credit losses - loans is based on: (1) an individual allowance for specifically identified and evaluated loans that management has determined have unique risk characteristics. For these loans, the estimated loss is based on likelihood of default, payment history, and net realizable value of underlying collateral. Specific allocations for collateral dependent loans are based on the fair value of the underlying collateral relative to the amortized cost of the loans. For loans that are not collateral dependent, the specific allocation is based on the present value of expected future cash flows discounted at the loan's original effective interest rate through the repayment period; and (2) a collective allowance for loans not specifically identified in (1) above. The allowance for these loans is estimated by pooling loans with a similar risk profile and calculating a collective loss rate using the pool's risk drivers, historical loss experience, and reasonable and supportable future economic forecasts to project lifetime losses. This collectively estimated loss is adjusted for qualitative factors.

Assessing the allowance for credit losses - loans is inherently subjective as it requires making material estimates, including the amount, and timing of future cash flows expected to be received on impaired loans, any of which estimates may be susceptible to significant change. In our opinion, the allowance, when taken as a whole, reflects estimated probable loan losses in our loan portfolio.

Net Interest Income. Net interest income represents the difference between the dollar amount of interest earned on interest bearing assets and the dollar amount of interest paid on interest bearing liabilities. The interest income and expense of financial institutions are significantly affected by general economic conditions, competition, policies of regulatory authorities and other factors.

Interest rate spread and net interest margin are used to measure and explain changes in net interest income. Interest rate spread is the difference between the yield on interest earning assets and the rate paid for interest bearing liabilities that fund those assets. Net interest margin is expressed as the percentage of net interest income to average interest earning assets. Net interest margin exceeds interest rate spread because non-interest-bearing sources of funds ("net free funds"), principally demand deposits and stockholders' equity, also support interest earning assets. The narrative below discusses net interest income, interest rate spread, and net interest margin.

Net interest income was $51.2 million for 2025 compared to $46.5 million for 2024. The increase was largely due to the impact of lower short-term interest rates which, with the Company's liability sensitive balance sheet (See Market Risk Section of the MD&A), resulted in lower deposit costs, a decrease in other borrowing expense due to lower balances and modestly higher net yield on assets. These increases to net interest income were partially offset by $61 million lower asset balances, including an $84 million decrease in average loan balances, partially offset by higher balances in lower yielding cash and cash equivalents.
The net interest margin for 2025 was 3.12% compared to 2.73% for 2024. The increase in the net interest margin was largely due to lower liability costs of 0.36%.

paragraphs: Citizens Community Bancorp, Inc. (the "Company") 為一間於 2004 年成立的馬裏蘭州公司。本公司為一間銀行控股公司，並受美國貨幣監理署 ("OCC") 與聯邦儲備銀行的監管。我們的主要業務為持有我們全資子公司銀行 Citizens Community Federal N.A. (the "Bank") 的股權，並透過該銀行提供商業、農業及消費性銀行服務。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們總資產約為 1.782 十億美元，存款約為 1.524 十億美元，權益約為 187.9 百萬美元。
該銀行為一間經美國聯邦政府核准的國家銀行，服務 Wisconsin 與 Minnesota 的客戶，透過 21 個全功能分行據點。其主要市場包括 Wisconsin 的 Chippewa Valley 地區、Minnesota 的 Twin Cities 與 Mankato 市場，以及這些地區周圍的各類鄉村社區。該銀行為企業、農業經營者與消費者提供傳統的社區銀行服務，包括一至四戶住宅抵押貸款。

我們維護一個網站於 www.ccf.us。我們透過該網站免費提供我們的年度報告 (Form 10-K)、季報 (Form 10-Q)、現況報告 (Form 8-K)、年度股東大會的股東權變更說明書，以及這些報告或文件的修正版本，於我們電子提交這些資料至美國證券交易委員會 ("SEC") 或提供這些資料給 SEC 後盡速提供。我們未將網站上或可經由網站取得的資訊納入本年度報告 (Form 10-K) 或以參考方式納入本報告。SEC 亦維護一個網站於 www.sec.gov，該網站包含有關 SEC 登記公司的報告、股東權變更說明書及其他資訊。

我們提供多種貸款產品，包括商業不動產貸款、商業及工業 (C&I) 貸款、農業不動產貸款、農業營運貸款、住宅抵押貸款、住宅貸款信用線及消費性貸款。我們依照銀行管理層所建立的基本貸款政策，並經董事會批准後，提供不動產、消費性、商業及農業貸款。我們的貸款業務主要針對我們市場區域內的個人消費者及小型商業借款人。我們的貸款業務歷來主要集中在 Wisconsin 與 Minnesota。我們的貸款市場存在競爭與經濟壓力，近期及未來任何發展在 (a) 總體經濟、(b) 不動產貸款市場、(c) 銀行業監管環境，可能對我們的業務與營運產生重大不利影響。這些因素可能影響我們現有貸款組合的信用品質，或不利於我們未來發放足夠高品質貸款的能力。

我們於 2025 年 12 月 31 日的總貸款餘額（扣除已核銷貸款成本及取得貸款的未償還折扣前）為 1.343 十億美元，其中商業/農業不動產貸款為 1.074 十億美元，C&I/農業營運貸款為 139.3 百萬美元，住宅抵押貸款為 123.8 百萬美元，消費性 installment 貸款為 6.2 百萬美元。有關我們貸款組合的進一步分析，請參見第 7 項；"管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析"，於 herein 之 "資產負債表分析" 項目下。
本公司維持一組投資組合，主要由房貸-backed證券、資產-backed證券、美國政府 sponsored 機構證券及企業債務證券組成。本公司試圖平衡投資組合，以管理利率風險、法規要求及流動性需求，同時提供與投資風險相稱的適當報酬。詳見第7項；"管理層對財務狀況及營運結果之討論與分析"，於"資產負債表分析 投資證券"標題下，有關投資組合之進一步分析。
存款。我們透過分行提供廣泛的存款產品，包括活期存款、各種儲蓄及貨幣市場帳戶以及存款憑證。存款由聯邦存款保險公司（"FDIC"）的存款保險基金（"DIF"）根據法定限額進行保險。於2025年12月31日，本公司總存款為1.524 十億美元，其中包括計息存款1.260 十億美元及非計息存款0.264 十億美元。
借款。除了本公司主要資金來源外，本公司亦透過借款取得額外資金來源，包括FHLB借款、與聯邦儲備銀行之信用線、本公司之循環貸款及聯邦資金購買信用線。詳見第7項；"管理層對財務狀況及營運結果之討論與分析"，於"資產負債表分析 聯邦住宅貸款銀行（FHLB）貸款及其它借款"標題下，有關借款之進一步分析。

本公司與其它金融機構及企業在吸引及保留存款及貸款業務方面進行競爭，於所有主要市場均如此。本公司認為，在競爭存款時，主要因素為利率、個性化服務、財務服務的品質與範圍、科技、便利的據點與營業時間，以及替代性的服務方式。其中一種服務方式為遠端存款捕獲，用於那些不便利前往分行的商業客戶，或零售客戶的行動銀行服務。存款產品的競爭主要來自於其他銀行、信用合作社及非銀行競爭對手，包括保險公司、貨幣市場及共同基金，以及其他投資選擇。本公司認為，在競爭貸款時，主要因素為利率、貸款發放費用，以及貸款服務的品質與範圍。成功的貸款發放往往不僅取決於利率與貸款條款，也取決於對客戶需求的靈活與回應。貸款的競爭主要來自於其他銀行、房貸銀行公司、信用合作社、金融公司、租賃公司及其他金融中介機構。一些競爭對手不受與國有銀行或 federally 保險機構相同程度的法規限制，這些機構可能能更積極地設定貸款與存款的價格。本公司亦面臨來自其他銀行及其控股公司的直接競爭，這些機構擁有較多的資產與資源。然而，本公司已能有效地與其他金融機構競爭，透過建立以小企業解決方案為重點的客戶關係，包括網際網路與行動銀行、電子付款及遠端存款捕獲。
銀行業受到高度規範，本公司與銀行皆受多項法律與法規的規範。作為銀行控股公司，本公司受美國聯邦儲備委員會（"FRB"）的規範、監督與檢查。銀行亦受聯邦儲備委員會（OCC）的規範、監督與檢查。銀行為聯邦儲備體系及聯邦住宅貸款銀行體系之成員。此外，銀行的存款帳戶由FDIC根據法律規定之最高額度投保，FDIC對銀行擁有某些執行權力。
以下為影響本公司與銀行之重要法律與法規之簡要總結。以下總結並非完整討論或分析，且全文應以所總結之法律與法規為準。適用於本公司與銀行之法律與法規可能有所變更。

paragraphs: 以下討論說明本公司管理階層對我們2025年12月31日財務年度及2024年12月31日財務年度之營運結果，以及2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日之財務狀況之分析。MD&A應與我們之合併財務報表、相關附註、選取財務資料及本10-K年報其他處所呈現之統計資訊一併閱讀，以獲得對以下討論與分析更完整的理解。除非另有說明，年份均指本公司財務年度，即2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日。
在比較年度營運結果時，淨利息收入、信用損失準備金、非利息收入及非利息費用的變動，主要由於上述所討論的項目。請參閱本節後續內容以獲得更詳細的討論。除非另有說明，本管理層財務狀況與營運結果分析中所列之表格（但不包括股數、每股及資本比率）之金額，均以千美元為單位表示。
本公司於2025年採用資產負債表最佳化策略，導致非戰略性貸款關係的減少，所得資金用以減少銀行之所有借款及減少 Wholesale 存款。
我們之合併財務報表係依美國通用會計準則（"GAAP"）編製。在編製財務報表時，我們必須對未來事件做出假設與估計，並應用影響資產、負債、收入、費用及相關揭露之判斷。我們的假設、估計與判斷係基於歷史經驗、當前趨勢及其他管理階層認為在編製合併財務報表時相關的因素。這些估計中，有些較為關鍵。以下為我們關鍵會計估計之討論。
我們使用損失估計方法及第三方模型，依循ASU 2016-13，財務工具－信用損失（主題326），"財務工具之信用損失衡量"，以決定我們之信用損失備抵金。請參閱經審計合併財務報表之附註1及附註3，以進一步討論我們對ASU 2016-13之採用。

信用損失備抵金－貸款。我們維持信用損失備抵金以吸收貸款組閤中可能且內在之損失。備抵金係根據貸款組閤中預期終身損失之持續、每季評估而定。在評估信用損失備抵金之水準時，我們考量貸款類型及貸款組閤中貸款金額、歷史損失經驗、可能影響借款人償還能力之不利情況、任何擔保品之預期價值、當前總體經濟條件及其他由管理階層所決定之相關因素。我們遵循所有適用之監管指引，包括由財政部國庫局、聯邦儲備銀行管理委員會、存款保險公司及國家信用合作社管理局所發佈之"信用損失備抵金跨機構政策聲明"。我們認為銀行之信用損失備抵金政策符合所有適用之監管要求。然而，根據監管機構之定期檢查，特定期間所記錄之信用損失備抵金金額可能調整。

本公司對於信用減損準備金 - 貸款的認定係基於：(1) 對於經管理層評估具有獨特風險特質且已明確識別之貸款，設立個別準備金。對於這些貸款，預估減損金額係基於違約機率、付款紀錄及擔保品之淨實現價值。對於依賴擔保品之貸款，其個別準備金係基於擔保品之公允價值與貸款之攤銷成本之間的關係。對於非依賴擔保品之貸款，其個別準備金係基於以貸款原始有效利率折現之預期未來現金流之現值；以及 (2) 對於未在 (1) 中明確識別之貸款，設立集體準備金。這些貸款之準備金係透過將具有相似風險特質之貸款歸類為一組，並計算該組之風險驅動因素、歷史減損經驗及合理且可支持之未來經濟預測，以預測整體生命週期之減損金額。此集體預估之減損金額已考量質性因素進行調整。
評估信用減損準備金 - 貸款係屬主觀性，因其需要做出重大之估計，包括預期於不良貸款上所收取之現金流金額及時點，任何估計均可能受到重大變動之影響。在本公司觀點，此準備金整體而言反映本公司貸款組閤中預期之貸款減損金額。
淨利息收入。淨利息收入係指利息收入與利息支出之間之差額，其中利息收入係指於利息產生資產上所賺取之金額，利息支出係指於利息負債上所支付之金額。金融機構之利息收入與支出會受到總體經濟狀況、競爭情形、監管機關政策及其他因素之顯著影響。
利率差與淨利息邊際率用以衡量及說明淨利息收入之變動。利率差係指利息產生資產之收益率與用以支應這些資產之利息負債利率之間之差額。淨利息邊際率係以淨利息收入與平均利息產生資產之百分比表示。淨利息邊際率高於利率差，因為非利息產生資金（"淨自由資金"），主要為活期存款及股東權益，亦支應利息產生資產。以下說明將討論淨利息收入、利率差與淨利息邊際率。

2025 年的淨利息收入為 51.2 百萬美元，較 2024 年的 46.5 百萬美元增加。此增加主要係因短暫利率下降的影響，配合本公司的負債敏感型資產負債表（請參閱 MD&A 中的市場風險部分），導致存款成本下降、其他借款費用因資產規模減少而下降，以及資產淨收益率略為提高。這些淨利息收入的增加部分被 61 百萬美元較低的資產規模所抵銷，包括平均貸款規模減少 84 百萬美元，部分抵銷因低收益率現金及現金等價物規模增加所帶來的影響。
2025 年淨利息邊際率為 3.12%，較 2024 年之 2.73% 為高。淨利息邊際率之增加主要係因負債成本下降 0.36%。

paragraphs: 下列所描述的風險並非我們唯一面臨的風險。我們可能還會面臨其他尚未知悉或目前認為不重要的風險，這些風險也可能影響我們未來的業務運作。如果下列風險中任何事件或情況實際發生，將可能對我們的業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大不利影響。在此情況下，我們普通股的交易價格可能會下跌。

我們的業務可能因金融市場狀況及總體經濟條件而受到不利影響。我們主要營運於威斯康辛州與明尼蘇達州市場。因此，我們的財務狀況、營運成果與現金流會受到這些地區經濟條件變動的重大影響。此外，我們的業務也易受美國經濟整體趨勢的影響。經濟條件會對我們產品與服務的需求產生重大影響，同時也會影響客戶償還貸款的能力、貸款擔保品的價值以及我們存款資金來源的穩定性。若因通貨膨脹、經濟衰退、貿易政策、關稅、失業率、證券市場變動、聯邦儲備委員會降息、房地產市場價格變動、國際政治不確定性、自然災害、疫情或其它因素導致總體經濟條件顯著下滑，將可能影響經濟條件，進而對我們的財務狀況與營運成果造成重大不利影響。

通貨膨脹可能對我們的業務及客戶造成不利影響。通貨膨脹風險是指投資資產價值或收入未來可能因通貨膨脹而降低，因為通貨膨脹會降低貨幣的價值。截至2025年12月的年度通貨膨脹率為2.7%，以消費者物價指數衡量。通貨膨脹會提高我們業務運作中所使用的商品與服務的成本，例如電力及其他公共設施，這會增加我們的非利息費用。此外，客戶也會受到通貨膨脹的影響，以及他們家庭與企業所使用商品與服務成本的上升，這可能會對他們償還我們貸款的能力或企業願意向我們貸款的意願造成負面影響。

國際政治緊張關係，包括現行或預期的軍事衝突影響，可能不利於總體經濟產業條件。國際政治緊張關係可能影響本公司營業收入。不利的經濟條件可能來自多種因素，包括國內與國際經濟與政治發展，包括內亂、恐怖主義、外資限制、各種政治或軍事行動，例如烏克蘭與俄羅斯之間的軍事衝突及美國及其他國家所施加的相應制裁，或中東及周邊地區的衝突，國際政治事件（包括中國與臺灣及美國與中國關係），以及新興或演變的法律與規範要求對商業投資、僱用、移民、勞動供應及全球供應鏈的影響。

本公司在商業與農業銀行業務方面面臨較高的貸款風險，可能不利於本公司財務狀況與營運結果。本公司貸款包括商業與農業貸款，包括以不動產為擔保的貸款以及以個人財產為擔保的貸款。商業不動產貸款，包括農業貸款，通常涉及較高的貸款本金金額，而這些貸款的償還通常 largely 依賴於不動產或在該不動產上進行業務的經營成效。商業不動產貸款可能更易受到不動產市場或總體經濟條件的影響。農業營運貸款具有顯著風險，因為它們可能涉及與單一借款人或相關借款人集中的較大貸款餘額。此外，這些貸款的償還依賴於擔保貸款的農場不動產的經營或管理成效。農業經營可能受到借款人無法控制的因素影響，包括不利天氣條件，例如乾旱、冰雹或洪水，這些條件可能嚴重限制作物收成，並導致農產品市場價格下跌。
此外，嚴重天氣事件，例如災難性火災、龍捲風或其他事件，可能影響我們所服務的市場，並對我們的客戶造成不利影響，例如阻礙借款人及時償還貸款，並降低我們所持有的擔保品價值。儘管銀行透過其授信與信貸管理政策來管理貸款風險，但無法保證這些風險不會實現，若發生此情況，可能對本公司財務狀況、營運結果、現金流及業務前景造成重大不利影響。
